newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius takes heart over new finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius takes heart over new finance minister.

text.p: Mauritian financial circles sighed with relief at the nomination of former parliamentary backbencher Vasant Bunwaree as finance minister in a reshuffle finalised by Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam late on Wednesday.
Bunwaree is a heart specialist, but his lack of formal training in economics or finance was not necessarily seen as a handicap by analysts.

"As long as the new minister is prepared to listen and follow advice from seasoned advisors in the finance ministry and the private sector and take good macroeconomic decisions, there is no reason to have any apprehension," independent economist Pierre Dinan told Reuters.
"Not every one is born an economist. This is something you learn and if he (Bunwaree) is willing to learn, why not?" said another economic observer who declined to be identified.
The chairman of the Mauritius Export Processing Zone Association, Francois Woo, was also happy with the appointment.
"A doctor always listens before making a prescription. His (Bunwaree's) capacity to listen is very important," he said.
In general, analysts were relieved there was now a minister able to devote all his attention to the country's finances.
In the reshuffled cabinet, Bunwaree is taking over the finance post from Ramgoolam himself, who replaced former finance minister Rundheersing Bheenick after the latter's resignation in early August.

The absence of a fully-fledged finance minister plunged the Indian Ocean island into political uncertainty from August to October and the Stock Exchange of Mauritius (SEM) index slipped to its 1996 low on October 23.

SEM Chairman Bruno Hardy told Reuters in late October: "For us, the sooner he (Ramgoolam) names a new finance minister, the better it will be. If the competence of the new finance minister is established, this will give back confidence to investment in the stock exchange."

Prime Minister Ramgoolam also restructured some of the government ministries during the reshuffle and created new ones such as International Trade, Land Transport, Public Safety and Public Infrastructures.
"Recognition is given to International Trade. This is a very important ministry, especially now we are now moving in an increasingly liberalised world trade environment," Dinan said.

Bunwaree was elected top of the list in the Mahebourg- Plaine Magnien constituency as a Labour Party candidate during the country's last general election in December 1995, but declined a ministerial post in Ramgoolam's first government due to professional commitments.
Bunwaree attended the University of Bordeaux in France from 1970 to 1981. In 1984, he was part of the team that performed the first open heart surgery in Mauritius.
Bunwaree entered politics in 1987, joining the Mouvement Socialiste Militant (MSM) of Anerood Jugnauth, Ramgoolam's predecessor, and entering parliament that year.
In mid 1990, he left the MSM to join the Labour Party and from 1991 to 1995 sat on the opposition benches with fellow Labour leader Ramgoolam.
